name: Brown Act Check
description: Checks a draft local agency agenda or meeting plan against a fixed Ralph M. Brown Act checklist (posting, descriptions, closed session, teleconference rules after SB 707). Checklist aid only. Not legal advice.
scope: draft agendas, notices and meeting plans of California local agency legislative bodies under the Ralph M. Brown Act (Gov. Code § 54950 et seq.)
input: the draft agenda or notice, the meeting type (regular, special or emergency), the meeting date and time, the posting date and time, and how each member will attend

starters.title: Check a regular agenda
starters.text: Check this draft regular meeting agenda against the Brown Act checklist. Meeting: [date and time]. Posted: [date and time].

starters.title: Closed session wording
starters.text: Compare these closed session agenda descriptions with the Gov. Code § 54954.5 model descriptions.

starters.title: Remote attendance
starters.text: A board member wants to attend remotely. Which teleconference rule applies and what must the agenda and minutes show?

starters.title: Special meeting notice
starters.text: Check this special meeting notice against Gov. Code § 54956.

items.check: Regular meeting: agenda posted at least 72 hours before the meeting, in a freely accessible location and on the agency website if it has one.
Each item, including each closed session item, has a brief general description (generally not more than 20 words). Flag any item whose staff report covers more than the description says.
Agenda states the time and location and says how to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
Agenda gives the public a chance to address the body on any item within its jurisdiction.

No action or discussion on an item not on the posted agenda unless one of three exceptions is found on the record: emergency by majority vote; need for immediate action that arose after posting, by two-thirds vote (unanimous if fewer than two-thirds are present); or item continued from a meeting held not more than five calendar days earlier.

Special meeting: written notice received by each member and each requesting media outlet at least 24 hours before, posted at least 24 hours before in a freely accessible location and on the website, stating time, place and business. No other business is considered.

Emergency meeting: the 24-hour notice and posting may be dispensed with only for an emergency situation; requesting media are notified one hour before (or, in a dire emergency, when members are notified).

Closed session: each item is on the agenda. Compare the wording with the model descriptions in § 54954.5. Before the closed session the body discloses the items in open session; afterwards it reconvenes and reports any reportable action and the vote.

Security or cybersecurity closed session: § 54957(a) covers a threat to critical infrastructure controls or critical infrastructure information relating to cybersecurity (added by AB 2715, effective January 1, 2025). § 54954.5 was last amended in 2012 and has no separate cybersecurity heading; the model heading for § 54957 is THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES with 'Consultation with:' the agency representative and title.

Standard teleconference: all votes by rollcall; agenda posted at every teleconference location; each location identified in the notice and agenda and open to the public; at least a quorum participates from locations inside the agency's boundaries.

Member with a disability attending remotely as a reasonable accommodation: audio and video (audio only if a disability-related condition requires it); the member discloses before any action whether anyone 18 or older is in the room and the general relationship; the member counts as attending in person, including for quorum; the location need not be on the agenda because subdivision (b) does not apply.

Alternative teleconference: allowed only in a circumstance listed in §§ 54953.8.1 to 54953.8.7 (health authority, proclaimed emergency, just cause with an in-person quorum, eligible neighborhood council, community college student organization, subsidiary body, multijurisdictional body). The body provides a two-way audiovisual platform, or two-way telephone plus live webcast; the agenda says how to attend and comment remotely; action stops during a broadcast disruption; the minutes list each remote member and the provision relied on.

Just cause remote attendance: a quorum attends in person at one location in the jurisdiction named on the agenda; the member gives notice and a general description of the reason; audio and video; yearly limit of 2, 5 or 7 meetings depending on how often the body meets. In effect until January 1, 2030.

Eligible legislative bodies (city council of a city of 30,000 or more, county board of a county of 30,000 or more, city council in a county of 600,000 or more, and listed large special districts): from July 1, 2026 every open meeting offers the public two-way telephone or audiovisual attendance and remote comment, with a disruption policy. Amended by SB 1187 effective September 18, 2026; in effect until January 1, 2030.
Writings given to a majority of the body less than 72 hours before the meeting are made available to the public when distributed.

If a violation may already have happened: a written cure-or-correct demand is due within 90 days of the action (30 days for open-session action that violated § 54954.2); the body has 30 days to cure; suit must follow within 15 days. State the rule and the dates given. Do not compute the deadline.
